ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Ida B. Wells — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Mrs. Wells comes for her subsequent annual wellness visit two weeks after starting dapagliflozin and four weeks after starting losartan for chronic kidney disease G3b A2 with hypertension. She has had no dizziness, faintness or genital itching and passes a little more urine than before. Her home blood pressure readings average 134/80. Her ankles no longer swell by evening, and she is less tired in the afternoons. Acetaminophen controls her knee aching and she has taken no naproxen since the first visit. Last week she went to the kidney education session at the health center, brought a page of questions, and asked to spend part of today on what the treatment options would mean for her if her kidneys failed one day. She has had no falls, emergency visits or hospital stays in the past year. [S]

Follow-up: Review in two weeks with potassium and creatinine. Mammogram, bone density scan and stool test as ordered. Next annual wellness visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1931-03-03: four weeks after starting dapagliflozin: potassium, creatinine and blood pressure, the losartan dose, and the plan for the months ahead. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 25 minutes, with her consent, building on the kidney education session. She understands that her kidney disease is at stage G3b and that, with treatment, most people at her stage do not reach kidney failure; the estimate of her own 5-year risk was explained as about 7 in 100. If her kidneys were to fail, she would want to be assessed for a transplant, would prefer home dialysis to center dialysis if dialysis were needed, and wants conservative kidney management explained to her again before any choice is made. She wants full treatment for illness that can be reversed. She has named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here. To be revisited yearly, at any sustained fall in eGFR below 20, or after a serious illness. [S]
